first.rationale:
Two of the three current problems are internal funnel decay (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%), and onboarding is the upstream cause of much of the activation drop. memory_86 and memory_31 both point at friction reduction, and memory_91 suggests activation messaging is a complement rather than a root-cause fix. So my current intent is simplify_onboarding, which addresses the shared upstream constraint rather than a symptom.

I am NOT choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor launch, for two reasons. First, memory_73 carries an explicit self-flagged defect: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so the reported acquisition/revenue lift may be an artifact of the redefinition rather than of price. That is exactly the kind of inherited claim that should not be scaled on. Second, the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue; discount-led acquisition against a competitor's entry pricing tends to import price-sensitive, low-retention accounts and reset price expectations for renewals. That downstream value risk is real even if memory_73 verifies clean.

Verification spend: memory_73 because it is the one memory that announces its own weakness and because it gates the most tempting alternative — if it verifies clean and the cohort issue was cosmetic, promotional pricing becomes a live option worth reconsidering next slot. memory_86 because it is the primary support for my intended action and I want to know what 'shortening onboarding' actually meant operationally (which steps were cut, on which segment, and whether the lift was in completion only or carried through to retained value). I am not verifying memory_31 even though it is adjacent, because if memory_86 holds, memory_31 is corroborating rather than load-bearing.

Residual uncertainty I am carrying rather than resolving: both memory_31 and memory_86 measure completion and early adoption, not durable qualified revenue. Removing signup fields and onboarding steps can lift completion while degrading qualification data, segment routing, and lead quality — which would hurt the actual objective while the dashboard looks better. memory_44 is a warning here: enterprise value flows through sales-assisted paths, so any simplification must be scoped to self-serve/SMB and must not strip the demo-request path or the firmographic fields that route enterprise prospects. I am therefore running this at standard experiment scale, segment-scoped to self-serve, with qualified-revenue and 30/60-day retention as gating metrics alongside completion, so a completion-only win does not get promoted as a success.
